requirements: R1: can_view returns True only when both tenant identifiers are present and exactly equal
R2: can_view returns False for different tenants and for any missing identifier
risks: auth.can_view (authorization decision): critical — an over-permissive result exposes another tenant's data
invariants: I1: no resource is readable across tenant boundaries

criteria.evidence: auth.py:2 never compares the tenants: can_view('tenant-a','tenant-b') -> True; no test covers it
auth.py:2: None or '' in either argument -> False; only (None,'tenant-a') is tested (test_auth.py:11)

selection_reasons.regression: release baseline (no consumers or preserved behaviors found; NO FINDINGS on interface, BLOCKER on I1 merged below)
selection_reasons.security: trigger: authorization / tenant isolation surface, risk critical

checks_executed.result: 2 tests OK (green with the cross-tenant bypass in place)

checks_executed.command_or_inspection: security reviewer authorization matrix (same / different / missing user / missing resource / both empty)
checks_executed.result: different tenants -> allowed (incorrect); the other four cases correct
removing the equality check (the shipped code) is uncaught; removing the presence check is uncaught

findings.claim: can_view grants access whenever both tenant identifiers are non-empty, without comparing them, so any tenant can read any other tenant's resources; R1, R2 and I1 are violated (merged with acceptance-1 and regression-1, same root cause)
evidence: test_auth.py:7-11 — no test with two different non-empty tenants
findings.failure_mechanism: can_view('tenant-a','tenant-b') -> True -> tenant-a reads tenant-b's data; no cross-tenant request is ever denied

findings.claim: No negative test for near-match identifiers (case or whitespace variants), so a comparison that normalizes case or trims would pass the suite
findings.failure_mechanism: a lenient comparison is introduced -> suite stays green -> a near-match tenant can read another tenant's data

evidence_gaps.evidence: E2: no test asserts that two different non-empty tenants are denied
E3 (partial): no tests for ('tenant-a', None) or ('', '')

minimum_next_action: Return user_tenant == resource_tenant only when both are present (auth.py:2) and add a test asserting can_view('tenant-a','tenant-b') is False
